transformations.edit: Replaced the seed string recorder with an executable Verus function for the Rust 1.96 target body.
Adapted the inherent mutable `[T]` receiver to an explicit `slice: &mut [T]` parameter, removed `const`, and named the return value for Verus; no target-body path was externalized or assumed.

Lowered the unsupported Rust slice pattern `if let [first, tail @ ..] = self` to the mechanically equivalent nonempty branch `slice.len() != 0`, `slice.split_at_mut(1)`, and `&mut head[0]`; this preserves the first-element/tail mutable data flow of the Rust body while using Verus-supported syntax.

Added proof-only `lemma_split_at` and view equality assertions before taking the returned mutable element borrow, connecting the desugared head/tail views to the generated `old(slice)@[0]` and `old(slice)@.subrange(1, len)` contract without changing executable control flow or data flow.
